revision_history: v1 (2026-05-31): initial draft after Phase 1 brief. Radar pick A3 (queue #100). Frame: graft at the payment-claims-approval gate, not at the tender award. RM7M project, RM1M allegedly solicited to release the contractor's claims, RM600k allegedly received (RM500k pre-Raya advance + RM100k at arrest). Suspect remanded, NOT charged.
_provenance.discipline: Process-not-people, presumption-of-innocence intact. MACC did not name the suspect or the statutory body; cards mirror that exactly. The circulating social-media allegation linking a named MP's office to the case (which that MP denied) is UNVERIFIED and EXCLUDED for defamation and irrelevance. No guilt asserted: 'alleged', 'remanded not charged' throughout. Cards report only MACC-stated specifics carried by two or more outlets including Bernama.

headline: A CEO was arrested not for rigging a contract, but for allegedly charging to release payment on one
context: On 13 April 2026, MACC detained the chief executive of an unnamed federal statutory body over an alleged bribe tied to a RM7 million squash-court project. The suspect was remanded for five days to assist the investigation and has not been charged.

cards.big: MACC arrested a statutory-body chief over a squash court, but the alleged bribe was not to win the job.
cards.sub: It was allegedly to approve the contractor's payment claims on a RM7 million project already awarded. The suspect, a man in his 40s, was detained in Bukit Jalil on 13 April 2026.

cards.big: The alleged ask was RM1 million to sign off claims; about RM600,000 is said to have changed hands.
cards.sub: MACC's account: RM500,000 paid as an advance before Hari Raya, then RM100,000 in cash at the arrest. No report states the full RM1 million was paid.

cards.big: He was remanded for five days to assist the probe, and has not been charged.
cards.sub: Magistrate Ezrene Zakaria issued the order in Putrajaya on 14 April 2026, running to 18 April. A remand is an investigation step, not a finding of guilt.

cards.big: The headline sum is small; the gate it guards is not.
cards.sub: Payment certification at a statutory body can rest on a single signatory's approval, the same choke point MACC has flagged across federal contracting.

cards.big: Watchdogs guard the tender. The money leaks one step later, where a single signature releases the cash on work already approved.
Whether this charge ever lands, the vulnerability is structural: the payment-approval step is where one person can quietly tax a contract the public already paid for.

sources: A1 Malay Mail 14 Apr 2026; A2 Bernama 14 Apr 2026; A3 FMT 14 Apr 2026; A4 The Star 14 Apr 2026; A5 The Edge 14 Apr 2026; A6 The Vibes 14 Apr 2026
confidence: High on MACC-stated specifics (RM7M project, RM1M solicited, RM500k advance, RM100k at arrest, five-day remand, magistrate Ezrene Zakaria, Bukit Jalil, suspect in 40s) — consistent across Bernama, Malay Mail, The Star, FMT, The Edge and The Vibes. The suspect and the statutory body are unnamed by MACC and remain unnamed here.
needs_verification: The 'single-signatory payment certification' characterisation (card 4 sub) is a structural generalisation, not a MACC statement about this specific body's controls. Stage 3 to confirm it is fair as a general statutory-procurement description or soften to remove any implication about this particular body's internal controls.
Confirm no outlet has since named the suspect or the body, or reported a charge, by the publish date — if a charge has been filed, the Legal card must be updated.
Confirm RM7M is the project value (not the contract sum to this contractor specifically) — Bernama/FMT phrasing to be re-read in Stage 3.
source_notes: AMOUNT: reports give RM500k advance + RM100k at arrest = RM600k of an RM1M solicitation; none assert the full RM1M was received. Copy says 'about RM600,000 is said to have changed hands' and 'No report states the full RM1 million was paid.' LABEL: Malay Mail says 'federal agency', Bernama/The Star/The Vibes say 'statutory body' — compatible; 'federal statutory body' used. EXCLUDED: FMT 15 Apr 2026 MP-link allegation is an unverified third-party claim the MP denied; not used (defamation + irrelevance).

_self_check.underclaim_check: Avoided. The MACC facts are stated plainly as MACC's account, not diluted to 'some say.'
_self_check.misleading_framing_check: The small-sum / large-gate contrast is the point and is stated as structural, not as proof against this individual. Remand is explicitly distinguished from a charge.
_self_check.unverified_detail_check: Suspect and body unnamed (mirrors MACC). The denied MP allegation is excluded entirely.
_self_check.process_not_people_check: Pass — the gate, not the man. No named person; structural vulnerability is the subject.
_self_check.anger_anxiety_check: Hook emotion is anger-at-process / anxiety-of-precedent (one signature taxes public work), not personal vilification.
_self_check.em_dash_check: No U+2014 em-dashes in reader-facing fields. Commas and colons used.
_self_check.auxiliary_verb_density_check: Verb-driven: arrested, win, approve, detained, changed hands, remanded, leaks, releases, guards, tax. No field stacks three+ auxiliaries.

pa_score_rationale: MACC-stated specifics are tightly multiply-sourced including a government newswire. Held below 85 because the story is pre-charge (outcome unknown, defamation-sensitive, so deliberately conservative framing), and card 4's structural claim about payment-certification controls is a generalisation flagged for Stage 3 rather than a sourced fact about this body.
